title: Espresso for the Reduction of Delayed Gastric Emptying After Pancreatoduodenectomy: RISTRETTO
summary: Delayed gastric emptying is a common complication following pancreatic surgery. It may delay the resumption of oral food intake, prolong recovery, and increase the length of hospital stay. This study aims to investigate whether regular consumption of espresso during the first three postoperative days improves gastric function and thereby promotes faster recovery. Previous studies suggest that coffee may stimulate gastrointestinal motility and improve digestion and the return to normal food intake. However, this effect has not yet been investigated in a randomized controlled trial following pancreatic surgery.
conditions: Patients scheduled for elective pancreatoduodenectomy for benign or malignant diseases

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Scheduled partial pancreaticoduodenectomy for benign or malignant disease.
Ability to understand the study procedures and comply with the study protocol.
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Planned or performed arterial reconstruction or total pancreatectomy.
Regular consumption of more than two cups of espresso per day.
Intolerance to espresso.
Congestive heart failure with a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <35%.
Sinus tachycardia (>100 beats/min at rest).
American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status classification > III.
Language barrier or cognitive impairment interfering with study participation
